title: A relative path literal resolves from the file that wrote it, and a relative path built at run time throws
scope:
Which directory a relative file path names when a program passes one to a `Core` member
or to a parameter marked `#[Core\Path]`, how the registry marks such a parameter, and the one member
that reads the working directory. How `nvs.toml` anchors a relative *grant* is unchanged.
dependsOnText:
[0021](0021.md) (`require` resolves against the requiring file), [0062](0062.md)
(path case), [0118](0118.md) (a path scope is compared after it is canonicalized).

summary.headline: Path literals are relative to their file
summary.body:
`Core\IO::read('data/x.json')` reads `data/x.json` beside the file that contains the call, in a
terminal, under `nvs serve` and as a service alike. A relative path built while the program runs
throws; `Core\Path::join` or `Core\Path::fromCwd` makes it absolute. Mark your own path parameter
with `#[Core\Path]` to get the same resolution.
